evidence_items.publisher: The New York Times, syndicated by The Indian Express
evidence_items.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Wendy’s, in an email to the Times'
evidence_items.explanation: The company statement supports the narrower point that human help remained necessary, while also showing that most orders were automated. The report additionally describes White Castle's almost-90% completion rate and McDonald's June decision to end its IBM trial, but supplies no complete staffing comparison.

The vendor framed the system as helping existing employees, which complicates the premise that complete job replacement was its intended purpose. The same account reports substantial order completion without human involvement, but predates the target quarter.

unresolved_gaps: No comparable staffing records establish whether automated ordering eliminated or substituted for complete positions.
The complete roles the systems were intended to replace remain unspecified.
The reported intervention rates do not measure how much employee time was required for exceptions.
